kick against the pricks phrase

also fight a losing battle, bang your head against a wall, it’s no use resisting, kick against the goad

classical

Ter. Ph. 77–78: Namque īnscītia est, adversum stimulum calcēs.
Lewis & Short s.v. stimulus: “kick against the pricks”

adversum stimulum calcēs

(to kick with) the heels against the goad: to make things worse by resisting

(vōx cōmica: Ter.)

The verb is left out in Terence. Plautus puts it another way: sī stimulōs pugnīs caedis, manibus plūs dolet (Truc. 4.2.55, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Namque īnscītia est, adversum stimulum calcēs.

    For it is folly to kick against the goad.Ter. Ph. 77–78

See also in vain, oppose, stubborn.

SourcesLewis & Short: stimulus

Terence, Phormio 77–78.
